summary: The Strategic Subsea Cables Act of 2026 aims to improve United States Government coordination regarding the security, installation, maintenance, and repair of critical undersea infrastructure, including subsea telecommunications and energy infrastructure. The bill establishes an interagency committee, mandates reporting on foreign threats and past sabotage incidents, requires new personnel at the Department of State, and directs the imposition of sanctions on foreign persons responsible for or facilitating sabotage of critical undersea infrastructure.

affected_groups.effect: Subject to mandatory economic sanctions, including blocked property and transactions under the International Emergency Economic Powers Act, as well as visa revocations and entry ineligibility.
affected_groups.group: Foreign persons, vessels, and entities involved in critical undersea infrastructure sabotage

affected_groups.effect: Engage in enhanced public-private information sharing regarding threats and participate with the federal government through newly coordinated operational frameworks and permitting processes.
affected_groups.group: Private sector owners, operators, and non-Federal entities involved in subsea telecommunications and energy infrastructu

affected_groups.effect: Required to participate in a new interagency committee, coordinate strategic oversight, develop response strategies, and submit multiple reports to Congress.
affected_groups.group: Federal agencies (State Department, Department of Defense, DHS, intelligence agencies, etc.)

key_provisions: Establishes a presidential interagency committee representing multiple federal agencies to lead efforts in protecting critical undersea infrastructure, improving resilience, and streamlining licensing and permitting processes.

Requires the President, in coordination with the Secretary of State and Secretary of the Treasury, to impose property blocking and visa revocation sanctions on any foreign person determined to be responsible for or facilitating sabotage against critical undersea infrastructure.

Requires the Secretary of State to increase U.S. engagement in international bodies like the International Cable Protection Committee and dedicate personnel and resources to work with foreign partners to reduce barriers to infrastructure maintenance and support a multinational fleet of cable repair ships.

Mandates several reports to Congress, including a Director of National Intelligence report assessing the causes and attributions of specific historical instances of critical undersea infrastructure sabotage, and regular reports regarding activities by China and Russia.

Directs the Secretary of State to assign at least 10 full-time equivalent individuals to critical undersea infrastructure expertise, with at least 5 assigned to the Bureau for Cyberspace and Digital Policy for subsea telecommunications infrastructure.

Directs federal agencies to issue procedures for timely, secure information sharing between the interagency committee and private sector owners and operators regarding infrastructure threats and sabotage indications.

The bill establishes an interagency committee, mandates reporting on foreign threats and past sabotage incidents, requires new personnel at the Department of State, and directs the imposition of sanctions on foreign persons responsible for or facilitating sabotage of critical undersea infrastructure.
summary_detail.significance: This legislation represents a sweeping federal effort to secure international subsea communications and energy pathways against foreign sabotage, enhance diplomatic coordination with allies, and establish formal public-private partnerships.
